question.problem: Write the following series in sigma notation: $40+20+10+5+….$
question.worked_solution:
The first term is ${a}_{1}=40$ and the second term is ${a}_{2}=20.$ Using these two terms, we compute the common ratio:

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{20}{40}=\frac{1}{2}
$$

Therefore, the general term can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{(r)}^{n-1} \\  & =40{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n-1} \\  & =40{(\frac{1}{2})}^{-1}{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n} \\  & =40(\frac{2}{1}){(\frac{1}{2})}^{n} \\  & =80{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as

$$
\begin{aligned}40+20+10+5+⋯ & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }80{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$
